name: Verizon Communications Inc.
executive_summary: Verizon screens as a Strong Buy on classic value metrics—P/E 10.7, P/B 1.9, dividend yield 6.4%, ROE 17.2%—with 13 of 22 models passing across cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk families. The investment case rests on a scaled US wireless and fibre franchise generating rising free cash flow, now complemented by an AI infrastructure narrative (dark-fibre deals, fixed-wireless access growth) under new CEO Daniel Schulman. Valuation embeds a sceptical view of low single-digit revenue growth and heavy leverage. The central debate is whether post-Frontier integration, subscriber momentum and cost transformation can sustain the dividend and a new $25bn buyback programme without further balance-sheet strain—particularly as total debt rose to $172.5bn at March 2026 per the Q1 10-Q, from $146.0bn at June 2025.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Verizon offers a rare combination of current income, depressed multiples and demonstrable cash conversion. The screen passes Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Magic Formula and Composite Value among others, with full data quality (20/20 metrics). That cheapness is not obviously inconsistent with business quality: reportable-segment operating income reached $32.2bn in FY2025 (10-K), up from $31.5bn in FY2024 and $31.1bn in FY2023, indicating stable core profitability beneath restructuring charges.

Operational trends support the screen’s quality and dividend buckets. H1 2025 consolidated operating revenues rose 3.4% to $68.0bn (Q2 10-Q), with Consumer up 4.6%; consolidated adjusted EBITDA for Q2 2025 was $12.8bn; H1 2025 free cash flow was $8.8bn. Q1 2026 showed continued momentum—consolidated revenues $34.4bn (+2.9% YoY), consolidated net income $5.1bn, adjusted EBITDA $13.4bn—though integration costs ($261m Frontier-related charges in the quarter) and a debt step-up temper the clean read-through.

The GARP element is emerging rather than established: fixed-wireless access broadband connections grew 34% YoY to 3.1m at June 2025, and management has pivoted messaging toward AI connectivity monetisation. At ~6.4% yield on a business with ~$19.7bn FY2025 free cash flow (Yahoo fallback—see Financial Review), the market prices Verizon as a bond proxy with limited growth optionality. If subscriber economics and enterprise fibre wins (Google dark-fibre deal, >$1bn per news flow) prove durable, the screen’s Strong Buy signal looks fundamentally anchored rather than purely contrarian.
financial_review:
**Source note:** Filing body extracts are truncated (80,000-character cap) and omit full consolidated income-statement and cash-flow tables for annual reports. Annual revenue, net income, EPS and FY free cash flow below fall back to `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo); all other figures are from SEC body extracts unless stated.

**Annual results (10-K, years ended 31 December)**

| Metric | 2025 (10-K) | 2024 (10-K) | 2023 (10-K) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reportable-segment operating income | $32,160m | $31,542m | $31,077m |
| Consolidated operating income | $29,259m | $28,686m | $22,877m |
| Income before tax | $22,672m | $22,979m | $16,987m |
| Interest expense | $6,694m | $6,649m | $5,524m |

FY2025 consolidated operating income rose 2.0% despite $1.7bn severance, $583m asset rationalisation and $91m acquisition/integration charges. FY2023 was distorted by a $5.8bn Verizon Business Group goodwill impairment (not repeated in 2024–25). Interest expense has trended higher since 2023, reflecting the leveraged capital structure.

**Yahoo fallback — annual revenue, earnings and cash flow**

| | 2025 | 2024 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | $138.2bn | $134.8bn | $134.0bn |
| Net income | $17.2bn | $17.5bn | $11.6bn |
| Diluted EPS | $4.06 | $4.14 | $2.75 |
| Operating cash flow | $37.1bn | $36.9bn | $37.5bn |
| Capital expenditure | $17.5bn | $18.0bn | $24.6bn |
| Free cash flow | $19.7bn | $18.9bn | $12.9bn |

Revenue growth re-accelerated in 2025 (+2.5%). Net income was broadly flat YoY on a reported basis; normalised earnings are cleaner ex-2023 impairment. FCF improved materially from the 2023 trough as capex normalised post-C-band buildout. Dividends paid were ~$11.5bn in both 2024 and 2025 (10-K cash-flow note), implying FCF dividend coverage of roughly 1.7x on FY2025 Yahoo FCF—adequate but not expansive once debt service is considered.

Balance-sheet figures (Yahoo fallback, 31 Dec 2025): total debt $181.6bn, net debt $139.1bn, tangible book value negative at −$85.9bn (goodwill/intangibles ~$190bn). Employee benefit obligations: $11.1bn. Cash and equivalents: $19.0bn.

**Interim results (10-Q)**

*Q2 2025 (three/six months ended 30 June 2025):*
- Consolidated operating revenues: $34.5bn Q2 (+5.2% YoY); $68.0bn H1 (+3.4%).
- Consolidated operating income: $8.2bn Q2; $16.2bn H1.
- Consolidated net income: $5.1bn Q2; $10.1bn H1.
- Consolidated adjusted EBITDA: $12.8bn Q2; $25.4bn H1.
- H1 operating cash flow: $16.8bn; H1 free cash flow: $8.8bn.
- Total debt at 30 Jun 2025: $146.0bn (effective interest rate 5.1%).
- Consumer postpaid phone net additions: −51k Q2 (improved from −109k prior year); FWA connections +34% YoY to 3.1m.

*Q1 2026 (three months ended 31 March 2026):*
- Consolidated operating revenues: $34.4bn (+2.9% YoY).
- Consolidated net income: $5.1bn.
- Consolidated adjusted EBITDA: $13.4bn.
- Free cash flow: $3.8bn.
- Frontier acquisition/integration charges: $261m.
- Total debt at 31 Mar 2026: $172.5bn (from $158.2bn at Dec 2025), reflecting Frontier closing.
- Board authorised $25bn share repurchase programme (Jan 2026, 10-K/Q1 10-Q).

*Q2 2026:* An 8-K was filed 27 April 2026 with earnings release exhibits, but no Q2 2026 10-Q body is yet in the filings index. News reports cite Q2 2026 revenue of ~$34.3bn and net income ~$3.8bn, with EPS beating consensus despite a revenue miss; management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS, FCF and buyback guidance alongside a >$1bn Google dark-fibre agreement. These Q2 2026 figures are **not** verified from filing body extracts and should be treated as provisional.

**Gaps:** Full annual income-statement and cash-flow line items are absent from truncated 10-K bodies. Q2 2026 interim filing body not yet available. Seven of nine indexed 8-Ks lack body extracts.
risks_and_flags:
**Leverage and interest burden:** Total debt increased sharply to $172.5bn post-Frontier (Q1 2026 10-Q). FY2025 interest expense was $6.7bn (10-K). At ~5.0–5.1% effective rates, further rate or spread widening would compress FCF available for dividends and buybacks. The company states it is in compliance with all restrictive debt covenants (Q2 2025 and Q1 2026 10-Q); no going-concern language appears in available extracts.

**Integration and transformation execution:** Frontier acquisition closed January 2026; Q1 2026 integration charges were $261m with elevated headcount and facility costs cited. FY2025 severance charges of $1.7bn and asset rationalisation of $583m indicate ongoing restructuring. Failure to deliver promised cost savings would weaken the value case.

**Competitive and secular pressure:** Business segment Enterprise/Public Sector revenue fell 3.1% in Q2 2025, partly from federal efficiency initiatives; filings warn these impacts “could be material” though not yet material to date. Wholesale wireline continues to decline on technology substitution. Wireless remains oligopolistic but pricing and handset subsidy cycles cap margin expansion.

**Legal and regulatory:** Filings disclose ~30 pending patent infringement actions; no individual accrual is material, but outcomes “could have a material effect on results of operations for a given reporting period” (10-K, 10-Q contingency language). Unrecognised tax benefits stood at $2.6bn at June 2025. Tariff and trade-policy uncertainty flagged in Q2 2025 MD&A.

**Pension and intangibles:** Periodic pension/benefit charges remain a recurring P&L item ($32m FY2025 per 10-K). Negative tangible book (−$85.9bn, Yahoo) limits P/B-based comfort and reflects acquisition-heavy accounting, not immediate liquidity risk.

**Governance transition:** CEO change to Daniel Schulman (October 2025) and interim Consumer Group leadership (February 2026) add execution uncertainty during a major M&A integration.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **heavy and recent**, clustered around Q2 2026 earnings (24–25 July 2026):

- **Q2 2026 earnings (24 Jul 2026):** Multiple outlets report EPS beat with revenue slightly light—e.g. “Verizon Communications (VZ) Q2 Earnings Surpass Estimates” (Yahoo Finance, 24 Jul 2026); “Verizon (VZ) Posts Mixed Q2 Results, Raises Full-Year Guidance” (GuruFocus, 25 Jul 2026).
- **Google dark-fibre deal (24–25 Jul 2026):** “Verizon Strikes Fiber Deal With Google Worth Over $1B” (TradingView, 24 Jul 2026); “Verizon Just Signed a More Than $1 Billion Dark Fiber Deal With Google” (Yahoo Finance, 25 Jul 2026). CEO cited additional billion-dollar-revenue deals expected by year-end.
- **Guidance raised (24 Jul 2026):** “Verizon Raises Guidance For Second Straight Quarter — CEO Says Carrier Is In Its 'Strongest' Operating Position In Years” (TradingView, 24 Jul 2026); “Verizon Communications (VZ) Raises Revenue and EPS Guidance for 2026” (GuruFocus, 25 Jul 2026).
- **Subscriber trends (24 Jul 2026):** “Verizon adds more than 550,000 connections, raises guidance” (Stock Titan, 24 Jul 2026); “Verizon (VZ) Reports Strong Q2 Postpaid Phone Gains and Improved Churn Rates” (GuruFocus, 24 Jul 2026)—partially offset by “Verizon stock rises as subscriber rebound comes with lower handset spending” (TechStock², 24 Jul 2026).
- **Cost restructuring (16–23 Jul 2026):** “VZ Stock Rises — Verizon Moves To Slash Costs With Major Store Shakeup” (Stocktwits/Yahoo Finance, Jul 2026); “Verizon Communications (VZ) Sells Stores And Cuts Jobs, Is The Stock Still A Bargain?” (Yahoo Finance, 23 Jul 2026).
- **Capital return (Jan 2026, per filings/news):** $25bn buyback authorisation; news cites ~$3.5bn repurchased YTD under the programme (Yahoo Finance, 24 Jul 2026).
- **Index removal (30 Jun 2026):** “Verizon Gets Booted From the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Is the Stock in Trouble?” (Yahoo Finance)—symbolic, not fundamental.
- **Management (2025–26):** Daniel Schulman appointed CEO; Hans Vestberg transitioned; Alfonso Villanueva Rodriguez named interim Consumer Group CEO (Feb 2026, 10-K).

Macro context (optional): US 10-year yield ~4.68% and policy proxy ~3.81% (macro_context.json, 24 Jul 2026)—relevant backdrop for a high-yield equity but not used to override the screen signal.
research_rationale: Deep research broadly confirms the quantitative Strong Buy on cash yield and valuation, but rising post-Frontier leverage, integration friction and mixed Q2 revenue temper conviction relative to the screen’s 82% composite score.
